summary: This is a Wikipedia article excerpt on Samsung Group, a South Korean multinational manufacturing conglomerate headquartered in Samsung Digital City, Suwon, and the largest South Korean chaebol. It covers the group's founding in 1938 by Lee Byung-chul, its diversification and entry into electronics, construction and shipbuilding, and its split into five business groups after Lee's death in 1987. The excerpt ends partway through the 1980s and 1990s history, so later sections are not included.
one_line: Overview and history of Samsung Group, the South Korean chaebol founded in 1938 by Lee Byung-chul and headquartered in Suwon.
key_facts: Samsung Group was founded by Lee Byung-chul on 1 March 1938 in Daegu, Japanese Korea.
Samsung Group is headquartered in Samsung Digital City, Yeongtong-gu, Suwon, South Korea.
Samsung Group is described as the largest South Korean chaebol (business conglomerate).
As of 2020, Samsung Group had the eighth-highest global brand value.
Samsung Electronics was the world's largest information technology company, consumer electronics maker and chipmaker measured by 2017 revenues.
Samsung Heavy Industries was the world's second largest shipbuilder measured by 2010 revenues.
Samsung Engineering and Samsung C&T Corporation were the world's 13th and 36th largest construction companies, respectively.
Samsung Life Insurance was the world's 14th largest life insurance company.
Cheil Worldwide was the world's 15th largest advertising agency as measured by 2012 revenues.
The Samsung name comes from hanja meaning 'three stars', where 'three' stands for big, numerous and powerful, and 'stars' for everlasting or eternal.
Samsung Group entered the electronics industry in the late 1960s, and its first product was a black-and-white television set.
The SPC-1000, introduced in 1982, was Samsung's first personal computer, sold only in the Korean market.
After Lee Byung-chul's death in 1987, Samsung Group was separated into five business groups: Samsung Group, Shinsegae Group, CJ Group, Hansol Group, and JoongAng Group.
As of 2012, Samsung had invested more than US$13,000,000,000 in the Austin facility, which operates as Samsung Austin Semiconductor.
